exposure: antenatal care service utilization (early registration of pregnancy, ANC visits, tetanus toxoid, IFAS consumption)
knowledge regarding early registration of pregnancy
permission to attend a health facility
ability to meet expenses of health care services
cohort: The study included 200 pregnant women aged 18-49 years residing in the field practice areas of a Medical College in South-East Delhi.
finding: The study found that 90% of newborns had normal birth weights, 81% of participants had NVDs, and identified knowledge regarding early registration and the presence of an accompanying person as enablers for ANC utilization, while permission for health visits, expenses for health care services, and distance to health facility were barriers.
mod_finding: 81.0% of participants had normal vaginal deliveries (NVDs) and 19% underwent caesarean sections.
cross-section timing: During or shortly after pregnancy (data collected on current pregnancies and newborns)
birth_weight: Normal birth weights and low birth weights were measured.
